requirement:
The table of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.table` MUST group
its listed files by their directory hierarchy. Each non-root directory
containing a listed file, directly or through descendants, MUST have a group.
Each group MUST be independently expandable and collapsible.

A collapsed group MUST show its workspace-relative path and the summaries
required by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.minimum` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.minimum.statuses`, while
hiding its file rows and descendant groups.
rationale:
The two tests marked for `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.directories` cover each obligation in its text. Both are in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`: `combined_directory_minimum_includes_hidden_passing_files` and `directory_minima_use_exact_fractions_and_count_unmeasured_descendants`. The summaries (minimum and not-measured count) are the tested subject of the refining requirements `.minimum` and `.minimum.statuses`, so I only checked here that a collapsed group shows them. - **Grouping by directory hierarchy.** The combined test builds `src`, `src/nested` and `src/nested/deep`. It asserts the parent/child nesting with `assert_directory_contents`. That helper uses `directory_group`, which matches nested `
` tags by depth. It checks that each child group sits inside its parent's body and that each file row sits inside its own directory's body. The test also checks that the root file `code.rs` appears before any `gap-directory` control, so root files are not grouped. - **A group for every non-root directory with a listed file, directly or through descendants.** - In the combined test, `src/nested` has no listed file of its own, only the descendant `src/nested/deep/gap.rs`. It still gets a group. - The second test adds sibling and prefix-like directories: `src/sibling`, `src-other` and `src/nested/deep`. Each has its own group, and the `src` group does not absorb `src-other`. - **Independent expand and collapse.** Each group is asserted to be a native `
` element. - The second test closes only `src/nested` by removing its `open` attribute. It then asserts that the `src` group stays open, that the `src/nested` group's content is unchanged, and that every file card is unchanged. - It also asserts that the closed and open maps differ only in that attribute, and that the summaries of all other groups are identical. - A browser cannot be run here. The tests therefore verify the structural property that makes native collapse work. - **A collapsed group shows its path and summaries, and hides file rows and descendant groups.** `assert_directory_contents` splits each group at ``. - The summary part must contain `{directory}/` (the path), must not contain `data-file=` or `` hides. I found no scenario that a violating implementation could pass. Rows or descendant groups placed in the summary are rejected. A missing intermediate group is rejected. A shared or non-independent open state is rejected by the sibling-state assertions. The `{test}` markings are present. There is no {fixme} acknowledgment, and none is needed.

text: :::{req} index.file_map.directories
The table of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.table` MUST group
its listed files by their directory hierarchy. Each non-root directory
containing a listed file, directly or through descendants, MUST have a group.
Each group MUST be independently expandable and collapsible.
A collapsed group MUST show its workspace-relative path and the summaries
required by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.minimum` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.minimum.statuses`, while
hiding its file rows and descendant groups.
:::{req} index.file_map.table
Each file coverage map MUST present its listed files in a compact table, with
one row per file and columns for its workspace-relative path and coverage
percentage or measurement status. Covered and instrumented line counts MUST
remain available in each measured file's row or expanded details.
The counts, statuses, and visual distinction of coverage levels MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`.
:::{req} index.file_map.minimum
Each directory group under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.directories` MUST display the
minimum measured file coverage percentage within its directory, including
descendant directories.
For the combined gaps overview, the minimum MUST consider all current
first-party Rust files represented by the map within that directory,
including files hidden because they have no unsatisfied obligations.
The minimum MUST use the file coverage fractions of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map` before rounding for display,
regardless of which groups are expanded. Its label MUST identify it as the
minimum measured file coverage. Not-measured and unavailable files MUST NOT
contribute a percentage. A group with no measured files MUST show no numerical
minimum.
:::{req} index.file_map.minimum.statuses
Each directory group under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.directories` MUST display
the number of its listed files, including descendants, that are not measured
whenever that count is nonzero. The status MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`. The count MUST describe
only files listed by the map, regardless of which groups are expanded.
